PORT

120minutes
28solder joints
difficulty

Local control and true status for your garage door

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    GNDController GND · Opener terminal GND · R2 divider 10k 2
    GDO_CTRLOpener terminal CTRL · RX MOSFET G · TX transistor C
    GNDRX MOSFET S · Controller GND.2 · TX transistor E · R3 pull-down 10k 2
    GDO_RXRX MOSFET D · Controller IO21
    GDO_TXController IO22 · R4 base 1k 1
    TX_BASER4 base 1k 2 · TX transistor B · R3 pull-down 10k 1
    GDO_OBST_RAWOpener terminal OBST · R1 divider 10k 1
    GDO_OBSTR1 divider 10k 2 · Controller IO23 · R2 divider 10k 1
  3. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  4. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
13PORT-WIRE-1

Port is built

Port is an open-source ratgdo interface (the rat-ratgdo v2.5 circuit) on an ESP32 D1 Mini, wired to the wall-control terminals of a Chamberlain or LiftMaster Security+ opener. It runs the upstream ESPHome ratgdo firmware and gives Home Assistant open, close, stop, position, light and obstruction state without a cloud account, while the wall button and the safety beam keep working as before.
